payload.system:
You are the learner in an experiment run with a formal evaluator, Residuum.

The theory LegalGeneral (Formal source below) is fixed; you cannot change it. You may add rules over its
existing verbs and constants. 3 dossiers are presented one at a time in a fixed order. A dossier is
a set of established facts (seeds). For each dossier the evaluator holds documented normative positions
(obligation, permission, prohibition, omissionProhibition or right over subject, conduct, object and
beneficiary), marked as required or excluded. They are not shown to you.

Each dossier has two phases.
- explore: you see the dossier and the closure Residuum computes for LegalGeneral plus your committed
  hypotheses, with justifications. This phase is for investigating the dossier: which relations it contains,
  what consequences possible generalisations would have, and how alternative hypotheses differ.
  propose_rule creates a draft hypothesis: a draft has no effect on your committed set R_k and is never
  scored. evaluate_rule tests a hypothesis hypothetically on a presented dossier, without penalty.
  Each draft that Residuum admits is evaluated at once, automatically, on the current dossier (one
  verified evaluation from the budget), and that evaluation is returned with the admission. You may
  draft, test, compare and discard as many alternatives as the budgets allow; discard records that you set a
  draft aside and why, and pose_question records a question if that helps you. commit is the decision to
  incorporate hypotheses into R_k so that they are contrasted with later experience; give its reason. When
  you end the phase, the committed set is scored on this dossier: loss = required positions not derived +
  excluded positions derived. Drafts you did not commit play no part in it. That prequential score is
  final and is never revised. The phase ends only after at least one draft in it or with a stated
  abstention; you are never required to produce a rule.
  During explore, judge hypotheses by how much they can tell you about formal consequences and differences.
  The normative loss does not apply to drafts or to their evaluations. Decide separately, at the end of the
  phase, whether to commit any hypothesis; you may commit none. Uncertainty about whether a hypothesis is
  correct is a reason to test it, not a reason to skip the test.
- revise: After each scoring you receive the list of discrepancies for that dossier: documented positions your committed theory did not derive, and excluded positions it derived with the hypotheses responsible. You may revise, keep or discard hypotheses (draft, test, discard and commit again),
  also when no dossiers remain. The changes apply to the following dossiers; every presented dossier is also
  rescored with the new committed set, recorded separately as a retrospective adjustment.

Your task: build and test hypotheses that could explain how the dossiers are treated, and commit those
you have reason to expect to hold. The evaluator contrasts your committed hypotheses with the documented
positions through the loss.

Budgets for the whole trajectory: 40 verified evaluations, 40
proposals, 30 turns per phase. Every turn is exactly one tool call.

Navigation tools give access to Residuum's own operations on the presented dossiers and your admitted hypotheses (theory inventory, forward and residual sessions, minimal supports, partition comparison). They never return valuations or loss. Budget: 60 navigation calls and 4000 engine steps for the whole trajectory. Sessions do not survive the presentation of a new dossier.

Findings: when you end a phase you may report findings about the space of hypotheses (end_phase, field
findings): what you established about relations, consequences or differences between hypotheses. Each
finding may carry an assertion that cites a record by its reference (n... for a navigation result, e... for
an evaluation) and is checked against that record by Residuum's existing claims verifier. Findings are
kept with their verdicts and shown in later views. They are separate from drafts and from the committed
set, they are never scored, and an empty report is valid.

LegalGeneral (fixed theory):
```
module LegalGeneral

// Extracción íntegra de la parte reutilizable no específica de compraventa.
// Los cuerpos y nombres proceden de case_monotonic_formal.res sin cambios.

entity Person {
    patrimony : Patrimony
}
entity Thing
entity Conduct
entity PerformanceMode
entity Relation {
    debtor   : Person
    thing    : Thing?
    conduct  : Conduct?
    creditor : Person
    mode     : PerformanceMode
}
entity Patrimony {
    assets      : Set Thing
    rights      : Set Relation
    obligations : Set Relation
}
entity Authority
entity Fact
const Doing : PerformanceMode
const Abstaining : PerformanceMode

const transfer : Conduct
const enact : Conduct
const use : Conduct
const private : Authority
const legislative : Authority
const judicial : Authority
const administrative : Authority
const constitutional : Authority

// oldDate y newDate son fechas simbólicas de vigencia, no números de ronda.
// tau indexa las proposiciones del expediente observado. No se identifica con
// la vigencia ni con DerivationTime. La comparación de fechas es un dato;
// no se presupone un orden de calendario ni que after sea sucesor discreto.
seeded verb Act(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
seeded verb right(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
seeded verb obligationFiled(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
seeded verb prohibition(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
seeded verb omissionProhibition(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
seeded verb permissionFiled(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
seeded verb extinguished(id : Fact, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)

// La misma compraventa puede estudiarse bajo dos paquetes aportados como
// datos positivos. reciprocity no selecciona defaults ni excluye otro paquete.
seeded verb higherAuthority(higher : Authority, lower : Authority)
seeded verb notEarlier(later : PropositionTime, earlier : PropositionTime)

seeded verb patrimonialHolding(id : Fact, owner : Person, object : Thing, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
seeded verb powerGranted(id : Fact, holder : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
seeded verb legislationText(act : Fact, norm : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)

// obligationFiled es el ingreso externo. obligation es la conclusión Derived
// común a ese ingreso y a las obligaciones que produzca law.
derived verb obligation(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb permission(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb compliance(norm : Fact, act : Fact, subject : Person, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb violation(norm : Fact, act : Fact, subject : Person, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb enforceability(norm : Fact, act : Fact, subject : Person, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb inconsistent(id : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb disputedPerformance(norm : Fact, act : Fact, subject : Person, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb patrimonialAsset(owner : Person, object : Thing, cause : Fact, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb patrimonialLiability(debtor : Person, object : Thing, cause : Fact, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb transferred(act : Fact, subject : Person, object : Thing, recipient : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb owns(owner : Person, object : Thing, cause : Fact, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb capacity(holder : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, cause : Fact, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb legislativeCapacity(holder : Person, object : Thing, cause : Fact, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb legislativePower(holder : Person, cause : Fact, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb law(norm : Fact, subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, object : Thing, beneficiary : Person, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)
derived verb annulled(inferior : Fact, superior : Fact, authority : Authority, effective : PropositionTime)

// Effects conocidos y State se mantienen separados. do/notDo constituyen
// relaciones de hacer/abstenerse; no son evidencia de una conducta histórica.
// mode es un campo ordinario del record, no una polaridad de Act.
effect verb give(subject : Person, object : Thing, recipient : Person) =>
    subject.patrimony.assets -= object
    recipient.patrimony.assets += object

effect verb do(subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, indirectObject : Thing?, beneficiary : Person) =>
    subject.patrimony.obligations += Relation {
        debtor = subject,
        thing = indirectObject,
        conduct = conduct,
        creditor = beneficiary,
        mode = Doing,
    }
    beneficiary.patrimony.rights += Relation {
        debtor = subject,
        thing = indirectObject,
        conduct = conduct,
        creditor = beneficiary,
        mode = Doing,
    }

effect verb notDo(subject : Person, conduct : Conduct, indirectObject : Thing?, beneficiary : Person) =>
    subject.patrimony.obligations += Relation {
        debtor = subject,
        thing = indirectObject,
        conduct = conduct,
        creditor = beneficiary,
        mode = Abstaining,
    }
    beneficiary.patrimony.rights += Relation {
        debtor = subject,
        thing = indirectObject,
        conduct = conduct,
        creditor = beneficiary,
        mode = Abstaining,
    }

// Reglas puente expresas del expediente. La norma queda en Known; su efecto
// puede ejecutarse después. Autoridad y vigencia se conservan en provenance.
rule obligationCreatesRelation(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, t) =
    obligation(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= do(subject, conduct, object, beneficiary) @ after t

rule prohibitionCreatesAbstention(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, t) =
    prohibition(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= notDo(subject, conduct, object, beneficiary) @ after t

rule historicalTransferEffect(act, subject, object, recipient, authority, effective, t) =
    transferred(act, subject, object, recipient, authority, effective) @ t
    <= give(subject, object, recipient) @ after t

rule filedObligation(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, t) =
    obligationFiled(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= obligation(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

// Los permisos externos y los producidos por reglas tienen la misma forma
// Derived. El documento sembrado permanece en Known, como obligationFiled.
rule filedPermission(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, t) =
    permissionFiled(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= permission(id, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

// Reciprocidad monotónica. El permiso es común a los dos paquetes; Plain
// añade el deber desde la compraventa, Retention lo condiciona al pago.
// t es el índice del expediente observado; effective conserva la vigencia
// de la norma y paymentEffective la del documento de pago, sin identificarlas.
rule obligationCompliance(norm, act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, actAuthority, actEffective, t) =
    obligation(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & Act(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, actAuthority, actEffective) @ t
    <= compliance(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

rule rightCompliance(norm, act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, actAuthority, actEffective, t) =
    right(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & Act(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, actAuthority, actEffective) @ t
    <= compliance(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

rule obligationViolation(norm, act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, actAuthority, actEffective, t) =
    obligation(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & ~Act(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, actAuthority, actEffective) @ t
    <= violation(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

rule rightEnforceability(norm, act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, actAuthority, actEffective, t) =
    right(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & ~Act(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, actAuthority, actEffective) @ t
    <= enforceability(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

rule prohibitedAct(norm, act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, actAuthority, actEffective, t) =
    prohibition(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & Act(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, actAuthority, actEffective) @ t
    <= violation(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

rule prohibitedOmission(norm, act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, actAuthority, actEffective, t) =
    omissionProhibition(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & ~Act(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, actAuthority, actEffective) @ t
    <= violation(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

// Marcas ordinarias del dominio. No dan prioridad a violation, no bloquean
// reglas y no generan otros hechos salvo los expresamente declarados aquí.
// La oposición exacta exige mismos argumentos e índice, incluida la metadata.
rule conflictingActEvidence(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, t) =
    Act(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & ~Act(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= inconsistent(act, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

rule performanceDispute(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, t) =
    compliance(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & violation(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= disputedPerformance(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t


rule violationLiability(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, t) =
    violation(norm, act, subject, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= patrimonialLiability(subject, object, norm, authority, effective) @ t

rule existingAsset(id, owner, object, authority, effective, t) =
    patrimonialHolding(id, owner, object, authority, effective) @ t
    <= patrimonialAsset(owner, object, id, authority, effective) @ t

rule patrimonyTitle(owner, object, cause, authority, effective, t) =
    patrimonialAsset(owner, object, cause, authority, effective) @ t
    <= owns(owner, object, cause, authority, effective) @ t

rule transferOccurrence(act, subject, object, recipient, authority, effective, t) =
    Act(act, subject, transfer, object, recipient, authority, effective) @ t
    <= transferred(act, subject, object, recipient, authority, effective) @ t

rule transferTitle(act, subject, object, recipient, authority, effective, t) =
    transferred(act, subject, object, recipient, authority, effective) @ t
    <= owns(recipient, object, act, authority, effective) @ t

rule ownershipCapacity(owner, object, cause, authority, effective, t) =
    owns(owner, object, cause, authority, effective) @ t
    <= capacity(owner, use, object, cause, authority, effective) @ t

// El poder legislativo exige su propio hecho de atribución: la titularidad
// de una cosa no confiere por sí sola poder para legislar.
// Su capacidad tiene un predicado distinto de la capacidad patrimonial de uso;
// así el grafo de dependencias del expediente es también explícitamente acíclico.
rule grantedCapacity(id, holder, object, authority, effective, t) =
    powerGranted(id, holder, enact, object, authority, effective) @ t
    <= legislativeCapacity(holder, object, id, authority, effective) @ t

rule capacityPower(owner, object, cause, authority, effective, t) =
    legislativeCapacity(owner, object, cause, authority, effective) @ t
    <= legislativePower(owner, cause, authority, effective) @ t

rule enactLaw(act, legislatorPerson, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, powerCause, powerAuthority, powerEffective, norm, subject, conduct, t) =
    Act(act, legislatorPerson, enact, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    & legislativePower(legislatorPerson, powerCause, powerAuthority, powerEffective) @ t
    & legislationText(act, norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= law(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

rule statutoryObligation(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective, t) =
    law(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t
    <= obligation(norm, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, authority, effective) @ t

// Conflicto sólo si coinciden sujeto, conducta, cosa y beneficiario.
// La superioridad debe ser estricta y la vigencia superior no anterior.
// Se consideran ambas orientaciones de permission/prohibition y
// obligation/prohibition. annulled añade una marca, jamás retracta el inferior.
rule permissionAnnulsProhibition(high, low, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, highAuthority, lowAuthority, highDate, lowDate, t) =
    permission(high, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, highAuthority, highDate) @ t
    & prohibition(low, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, lowAuthority, lowDate) @ t
    & higherAuthority(highAuthority, lowAuthority) @ t
    & notEarlier(highDate, lowDate) @ t
    <= annulled(low, high, highAuthority, highDate) @ t

rule prohibitionAnnulsPermission(high, low, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, highAuthority, lowAuthority, highDate, lowDate, t) =
    prohibition(high, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, highAuthority, highDate) @ t
    & permission(low, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, lowAuthority, lowDate) @ t
    & higherAuthority(highAuthority, lowAuthority) @ t
    & notEarlier(highDate, lowDate) @ t
    <= annulled(low, high, highAuthority, highDate) @ t

rule obligationAnnulsProhibition(high, low, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, highAuthority, lowAuthority, highDate, lowDate, t) =
    obligation(high, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, highAuthority, highDate) @ t
    & prohibition(low, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, lowAuthority, lowDate) @ t
    & higherAuthority(highAuthority, lowAuthority) @ t
    & notEarlier(highDate, lowDate) @ t
    <= annulled(low, high, highAuthority, highDate) @ t

rule prohibitionAnnulsObligation(high, low, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, highAuthority, lowAuthority, highDate, lowDate, t) =
    prohibition(high, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, highAuthority, highDate) @ t
    & obligation(low, subject, conduct, object, beneficiary, lowAuthority, lowDate) @ t
    & higherAuthority(highAuthority, lowAuthority) @ t
    & notEarlier(highDate, lowDate) @ t
    <= annulled(low, high, highAuthority, highDate) @ t

// Escenarios independientes del mismo programa, sin hechos fabricados en Rust.
```

  rule <name>(<param>, ...) =
      <atom> [& <atom>]...
      <= <head atom>

An atom is <verb>(<arg>, ...) @ <time>; a negative atom is ~Act(...) @ <time> (only Act may be
negated). Arguments are parameters or declared constants. Times are a parameter, a constant or
`after <param>`. Every parameter of the head must occur in the body. Rule names must be new.
Head verbs allowed: obligation, permission, prohibition, omissionProhibition, right, compliance, violation, enforceability, patrimonialLiability. Body verbs allowed: Act, right, obligationFiled, prohibition, omissionProhibition, permissionFiled, patrimonialHolding, powerGranted, legislationText, obligation, permission, compliance, violation, enforceability, patrimonialAsset, patrimonialLiability, transferred, owns, capacity, law. At most 4 body atoms and
2 rules per proposal. Constants must be declared in LegalGeneral or occur in a dossier
already presented.

tools.name: propose_rule
tools.description: Create a draft hypothesis from Formal rule declarations. Residuum parses, elaborates and admits it or reports why not. A draft has no effect on the committed set R_k and is never scored. When the draft is admitted, Residuum evaluates it at once on the current dossier (one verified evaluation from the budget) and returns that evaluation.

text.description: One or more Formal rule declarations.

parent.description: Id of a hypothesis this one revises, if any.

tools.name: evaluate_rule
tools.description: Test a hypothesis hypothetically: the closure of LegalGeneral plus the committed hypotheses plus this one on a presented dossier, with Residuum's independent certificate. No penalty; uses one verified evaluation from the budget. Returns certificate status, its baseline (LegalGeneral plus the other committed hypotheses), the events it adds to that baseline, the justifications it contributes (each with its rule and the hypothesis that owns it, also on events the baseline already derives) and the positions that depend on its rules; never valuations or loss. Each verified evaluation also lists minimal supports. Its goals are the events the hypothesis adds or newly justifies over that baseline, ordered as added events first, then positions, then other verbs, then by text (a presentation order, nothing more). For each answered goal it gives every minimal set of this dossier's seeds from which the baseline plus the hypothesis derives it, with no search limit. Goals beyond the stated goal_limit or the support budget are listed as omitted.

tools.name: commit
tools.description: Decide which hypotheses form the committed set R_k (it replaces the current one). Committed hypotheses are scored and contrasted with later dossiers. The new theory must certify on every presented dossier.

reason.description: Why you commit this set (recorded only).

tools.name: end_phase
tools.description: End the current phase. Ending an explore phase triggers the scoring of the current dossier with the committed set. An explore phase ends only after at least one proposal in that phase or with a stated abstention.

abstention.description: Why you end this explore phase without proposing.

findings.description: Optional report of findings (it may be empty). Each item: kind, text and assertion (null, or {ref, attribute, value}).

ref.description: n... or e... reference of a record.

tools.name: discard
tools.description: Record that you set a hypothesis aside and why. It executes nothing and does not change the committed set.

tools.name: pose_question
tools.description: Record an investigable question about the presented dossiers and the theory, and the tool you will use to answer it. It executes nothing.

tool.description: Name of the tool you will consult to answer it.

tools.name: inspect_theory
tools.description: Inventory of the theory: rules with their bodies, verbs with signatures and kinds, entities, constants and the presented dossiers.

tools.name: begin_forward
tools.description: Open a forward session: the closure of a dossier under a theory, advanced round by round with advance_session (each round lists added events and their derivations).

hypothesis.description: Id of an admitted hypothesis: the theory is LegalGeneral plus that hypothesis. Null or absent: LegalGeneral alone.

tools.name: begin_residual
tools.description: Open a residual (backward) query session for a goal on a dossier under a theory: what is missing for the goal to hold, as search trees and residual conditions. Advance it with advance_session.

hypothesis.description: Id of an admitted hypothesis: the theory is LegalGeneral plus that hypothesis. Null or absent: LegalGeneral alone.

goal.description: One event in Formal, e.g. verb(arg, ...) @ time; ~Act(...) @ time for a negative Act.

bindings.description: Optional typed parameter bindings in the worker wire format.

tools.name: begin_active_residual
tools.description: As begin_residual, over the active (program) residual search.

hypothesis.description: Id of an admitted hypothesis: the theory is LegalGeneral plus that hypothesis. Null or absent: LegalGeneral alone.

goal.description: One event in Formal, e.g. verb(arg, ...) @ time; ~Act(...) @ time for a negative Act.

tools.name: advance_session
tools.description: Advance an open forward or residual session by at most max_steps engine steps.

tools.name: minimal_supports
tools.description: Minimal sets of seeded facts, over the presented dossiers, from which LegalGeneral plus the hypothesis derives the goal.

goal.description: One event in Formal, e.g. verb(arg, ...) @ time; ~Act(...) @ time for a negative Act.

tools.name: compare_partition
tools.description: Compare two or more hypotheses on a goal: the pool of minimal supports, which hypotheses derive the goal from each (signatures), the supports that discriminate them, and inclusion between their regions.

goal.description: One event in Formal, e.g. verb(arg, ...) @ time; ~Act(...) @ time for a negative Act.

uncertainties: Which positions the evaluator documents for brookside: likely obligations and rights of jant toward usa (policy adoption, distribution, posting, availability), a prohibition on usa suing, possibly permissions.
Whether reciprocity is expected: jant's obligations conditional on or paired with usa's counter-duty, or usa's rights mirroring jant's obligations (right derived from obligation).
Whether compliance, violation or enforceability should be derived. Act(saB_j ... agree ...) has a different conduct and object from the obligations, so exact-match compliance does not fire.
Whether an omissionProhibition or a permission should be derived for usa, for example a permission to sue under a different condition.
Whether the rules should generalise across later dossiers (casaFiesta, other persons), so they need to use variables rather than dossier-specific constants.

operations.purpose: Confirm rules, verbs and the dossier list at low cost.
Draft a general rule such as obligationFiled(id,s,c,o,b,a,e)@t => right(id,b,c,o,s,a,e)@t (creditor right mirroring obligation), and a variant for the prohibition giving omissionProhibition.
See which new events and positions each draft adds on brookside.
Compare the alternatives on a goal such as right(...) to see which supports discriminate them.
Ask what is missing for goals such as violation or compliance of saB_j.

distinguishing_results: A draft that adds right(...) events for usa only, versus one that also adds excluded-looking extras such as permissions.
Whether the mirror right triggers rightEnforceability or compliance, which would add more derived positions and more risk of excluded positions.
Whether the prohibition-to-omissionProhibition draft adds only the usa/sue position.
conditions: Continue if a draft adds a small number of well-motivated positions that follow the normative structure of the seeded facts.
Change the plan if drafts produce many side-effect events such as violations and liabilities that look excluded.
Abstain from committing if no draft is better than the empty set, since the empty committed set is a safe baseline. Commit only the minimal, general rule, and wait for revise feedback to refine it.

uncertainties: casaFiesta has no obligations, prohibitions or rights as seeds. It has only Acts: the agreement acts, plus casaFiesta adopting a policy and posting a sign for usa. So the documented positions probably come from a rule that turns these into obligations or rights.

Whether the documented positions are obligations and rights for casaFiesta (adoptPolicy on policyCF, post on signCF), matching the brookside structure. Brookside's obligations were filed seeds, but here there are none.

Whether the agreement Acts (saCF_c, saCF_u) should generate obligations, for example casaFiesta owes the policy conduct and usa gets a prohibition on suing, mirroring brookside. The policy conduct is only visible through the cfA1 and cfA2 Acts.

Whether compliance should be derived. This needs an obligation whose conduct and object match an Act. The Acts cfA1 and cfA2 match adoptPolicy/policyCF and post/signCF, so an obligation rule would make compliance fire. The id of the norm would have to be saCF_c or cfA1 to line up.

How far a rule generalises. Brookside's compliance did not fire because the Act conduct was 'agree', while the obligations concerned other objects. Any rule must avoid excluded violations, for example an obligation for distribute or keepAvailable with no matching Act would produce a violation.

operations.purpose: Draft a rule that derives an obligation from an agreement Act plus a performance Act, for example Act(agree) and Act(adoptPolicy) giving obligation(adoptPolicy), and check the new events. A draft is evaluated at once on casaFiesta.
Test the draft together with h2 on casaFiesta to see whether compliance, right, or violation events appear. Also re-test on brookside to confirm there are no side effects.
Ask what is missing for the goal compliance(...) or right(casaFiesta, adoptPolicy, policyCF, usa), to see which body atoms the rules need.
Compare variants, such as one deriving only obligations versus one deriving obligations plus an usa prohibition, on a shared goal.

distinguishing_results: A rule that yields compliance events for cfA1 and cfA2 with no violations, as opposed to one that yields violations (excluded risk).
Whether h2 turns the new obligations into rights for casaFiesta, so one rule covers both the obligation and the right positions.
Whether the draft fires on brookside, where there are no performance Acts, which shows if it is restricted to casaFiesta-like cases.
conditions: Continue if a draft derives obligations, rights and compliance for casaFiesta without violations.
Change the plan if the draft produces excluded-looking violations or liabilities; narrow the body.

Abstain, committing nothing new and keeping h2, if no draft clearly follows from the seeds. The brookside feedback shows only rights were documented, so a conservative rule is better than a broad one.
